implementation_notes: Kotlin makes the deadline part of the call structure: withTimeout wraps handling in a child coroutine that is cancelled with TimeoutCancellationException when the limit is reached, withTimeoutOrNull turns the same event into a null result, and one can pre-check a monotonic deadline with TimeStep.TimeSource.Monotonic (markNow().elapsedNow()) before doing expensive work. That replaces a broker TTL for work inside the process, and because coroutine cancellation is cooperative a handler that never suspends is not stopped - so the absolute deadline has to be re-checked before side effects. When messages cross a broker, keep the JMS/Jakarta time-to-live on the producer (Kotlin calls the same Java API) and treat the coroutine timeout as the consumer-side guarantee.
pitfalls: TimeoutCancellationException is a CancellationException: a catch (e: Exception) or runCatching block around the handler swallows it and turns expiry into silent processing.
withTimeout cancels only at suspension points, so blocking calls (JDBC, Thread.sleep, runBlocking) run to completion past the deadline; check the monotonic deadline before irreversible work.
A timeout on a hot path allocates a child coroutine and a scheduled cancellation; a shared expired-batch sweep with a deadline index is cheaper than one timeout per message.
